# SHYFEM Code Review — Final Report

**Scope:** SHYFEM v8.2.0 — Fortran hydrodynamic model + C utilities + Python Shiny UI (`shyfem-ui`)
**Method:** Multi-dimension deep review with adversarial verification of all high/critical findings.

---

## 1. Executive summary

The codebase is broadly healthy and well-instrumented, but the review confirmed **53 distinct issues**: **0 critical, 8 high, 25 medium, and 20 low** (severities below reflect verifier-adjusted values where a verdict downgraded the original rating). The Python UI carries a real **cross-user file-read / IDOR** class of bug — `validate_path` confines reads to the *shared* `work_dir`, the entire `shyfem_dir` source tree, and `/tmp`, never the requesting user's home — and several postprocess/visualize handlers read fully attacker-controlled paths after only an *active-project* access check. The single most important thing to fix is this **path-confinement gap (config.py:261-308 + the decoupled access checks in postprocess.py/visualize.py)**: it is reachable by any authenticated user in the documented prod (multi-user, server-mode) deployment and lets one tenant read another tenant's model data. The most severe Fortran defect is a **PETSc double-assembly of the zeta matrix** (`hydrodynamic.f90:616-771/780-870`) that silently produces wrong free-surface solutions whenever flux boundary conditions are present.

**Severity counts (post-verification):** High = 8 · Medium = 25 · Low = 20.

## 3. Detailed findings

### Critical

None confirmed.

---

### High

#### H1 — Cross-user file read / IDOR via unconfined `validate_path` (+ decoupled access checks)
**Files:** `shyfem-ui/shyfem_ui/config.py:261-308` and `shyfem-ui/shyfem_ui/pages/postprocess.py:395-416` (same root cause; merged).

**What's wrong.** `validate_path()` builds its allowlist as `allowed_roots = [self.work_dir.resolve(), self.shyfem_dir.resolve(), Path("/tmp").resolve()]` (config.py:291) — the *global* shared work dir, the entire source tree, and world-shared `/tmp`. It never confines reads to the requesting user's home (`user_data_root/{username}`). The per-user isolation model exists (`User.home_dir` at user.py:51, `config.user_data_root` at config.py:42) but is wired into neither `validate_path` nor `validate_save_path`. Because all projects are physically created under the single shared `work_dir` (see M2), every user's data co-locates under one root.

The authorization is provably decoupled from the read target. In `visualize.py:486-488` the gate `editor_denied_reason(_proj["id"], _usr, min_role="viewer")` runs against the **active** project, then `visualize.py:494/501` reads `input.data_path()` (arbitrary free text) validated only by `validate_path`. The same pattern recurs in `postprocess.py` `_scan_file` (398-416): `shy_path = input.shy_path()` → `config.validate_path(...)` → `wrapper.run_command("shyelab", ["-info", str(path)], path.parent)` with **no** ownership/project check on the resolved path; stdout/stderr and parsed metadata (variables, layer depths, time ranges) are streamed back. The same decoupling appears in `postprocess.py:404/498`, `compare.py:260-282`, `ensemble.py:420/527`, `ibm.py:416`, `grid_prep`, and `partitioning`.

**Why it matters.** Server/multi-user mode is the documented prod deployment (laguna.ku.lt). Any authenticated user with viewer rights on their own project passes the gate, then supplies another user's project path (under shared `work_dir`), anything under `shyfem_dir`, or any `/tmp` file, and reads/postprocesses it. This is an authenticated cross-tenant information disclosure (IDOR).

**Evidence.** config.py:291; visualize.py:486/494/501; postprocess.py:398/404/412. Verified high — could not be refuted; access-check sites in postprocess (485, 590, 749, 1115) are all in *other* handlers, never `_scan_file`.

**Fix.** Add a per-user confinement parameter to `validate_path`/`validate_save_path` restricting authenticated reads/writes to `user_data_root/{username}` plus read-only `shyfem_dir` assets; drop `/tmp` from the general read allowlist. Resolve the user path, look up the project that *owns* it, and enforce `editor_denied_reason`/`check_project_access` against that project — not the active one. Allocate project work dirs under the owner's home (see M2).

---

#### H2 — `jobs` table grows unbounded (LocalJobQueue): cleanup only sees the in-memory window
**File:** `shyfem-ui/shyfem_ui/services/job_local.py:441-487, 80-93, 205-218`.

**What's wrong.** `cleanup_old_jobs()` builds its delete list exclusively by iterating `self._jobs` (line 446) and deletes only those rows via `_delete_job_rows` → `Job.job_uuid.in_(to_remove)` (471, 485). But `self._jobs` is an in-memory `OrderedDict` (a) loaded at startup with only the 500 most-recent rows (`order_by(created_at.desc()).limit(MAX_STORED_JOBS=500)`, lines 88/42) and (b) trimmed back to 500 by `_evict_old_jobs`, which only does `self._jobs.pop(job_id, None)` (217-218) and never deletes the DB row. `_persist_job` writes a row per submission and never removes one. No age-based DB sweep exists.

**Why it matters.** Any persisted row older than the most-recent-500 window — exactly the set most likely to exceed the 30-day retention cutoff — is never a deletion candidate. The table grows by one row per submission forever while memory stays at 500. This matches the operational fact that prod had to be manually pruned (8644 → 0). (The Celery variant is unaffected: it builds `removed_uuids` from the full Redis zset.)

**Fix.** Make `cleanup_old_jobs` delete by age directly, independent of the dict: `db.query(Job).filter(Job.created_at < cutoff, Job.status.in_(terminal_states)).delete(synchronize_session=False)`, then reconcile/evict the dict separately. Also delete the DB row inside `_evict_old_jobs` (or rely solely on the age sweep).

---

#### H3 — PETSc path double-assembles the zeta matrix, corrupting the solution with flux BCs
**File:** `src/shyfem/hydrodynamic.f90:616-771 and 780-870`.

**What's wrong.** In `hydro_zeta` the subset/OMP loop (`do isubset=1,subset_num … call system_assemble_omp`) runs unconditionally for every element. For PETSc, `buse_omp` is set `.false.` (line 599), but it only gates the `!$OMP PARALLEL IF(buse_omp)` clause (605) — per OpenMP semantics `IF(.false.)` runs the region serially with a one-thread team; the `SINGLE/TASK/TASKWAIT` body still executes. `subset_num` is populated unconditionally at startup (`shyfem_subs.f90:366` → `domain_clusterization`), so the loop is non-empty regardless of solver. The PETSc-only serial loop at 780-870 then assembles every element **again**. `system_assemble_omp → add_matvec_values` uses `ADD_VALUES` for both `MatSetValues` (mod_petsc_system.f90:473) and `VecSetValues` (479), so element matrix A and element RHS `b_elem` accumulate twice into the matrix zeroed once before `hydro_zeta`. The flux-BC term `system_add_rhs(dt,nkn,vqv)` (880) is added only once.

**Why it matters.** The solved system is `2A·z = 2·b_elem + b_flux`, whose solution differs from `A·z = b_elem + b_flux` whenever flux BCs (`vqv`) are non-zero — a common, physically essential BC for coastal/estuarine runs. Zeta is solved incorrectly, and every element is assembled twice (doubled assembly cost) even without flux BCs. Affects PETSC builds only (default SOLVER=SPARSKIT is unaffected). The same duplicate-assembly pattern exists in `nohydro.f90:636`.

**Evidence.** `solver_type=='PETSc'` is compile-time-coupled to the PETSc build (simsys_petsc.f90:146; Makefile:114-118). Survived six refutation angles.

**Fix.** Skip the subset/OMP assembly loop entirely when PETSc is selected (wrap the `do isubset` body in `if(buse_omp)` / `if(solver_type/='PETSc')`). Add a regression test comparing PETSc vs SPARSKIT zeta on a case with a non-zero flux boundary.

---

#### H4 — Munk-Anderson closure raises a negative base to a fractional power → NaN/SIGFPE
**File:** `src/shyfem/turbulence.f90:185-207`.

**What's wrong.** In the iturb=3 (`munk_anderson_shell`) path, `ri = buoyf2(l,k)/shearf2(l,k)` is taken with the *only* guard being `shearf2 > 0` — no lower clamp on `ri`. `buoyf2` is N², which `setm2n2` (1034-1037) computes negative under unstable stratification (`rhov(l) > rhov(l+1)`). With `a=10.` and `alpha=-1./2.`, `(1.+a*ri)**alpha` has a negative base whenever `ri < -0.1` (likewise the `dif` term with `beta=-3./2.`), and a negative real base raised to a non-integer power is undefined.

**Why it matters.** gfortran evaluates `x**y` as `exp(y*log(x))`; `log` of a negative raises IEEE invalid. Under the default NORMAL build (`-ffpe-trap=…,invalid`) this SIGFPEs; otherwise NaN propagates into `visv/difv` (eddy viscosity/diffusivity), corrupting the entire hydro step. Convective/unstable stratification is routine in coastal/lagoon thermal dynamics, so `ri<0` is common once iturb=3 is selected. The mild caveat: iturb=3 is opt-in (GOTM/iturb=1 is the typical default), but once selected the crash path is routine.

**Fix.** Guard the base: `argv = max(1.+a*ri, tiny); vis = vistur_c*argv**alpha`, or clamp `ri`. Physically, the Munk-Anderson stable power law is only defined for `Ri≥0`; negative `Ri` should select an enhanced-mixing branch.

---

### Medium

#### M1 — Security/auth E2E never run on pushes to main *(verifier-adjusted high→medium)*
**File:** `.github/workflows/ui-ci.yml:67-89`. The Playwright suite is excluded from the unit job (`--ignore-glob=tests/test_playwright_*.py`, line 57 / pyproject:86) and the dedicated `e2e` job is gated `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (line 70). These E2E files are the only end-to-end coverage of prod auth/identity paths (login/logout, admin user CRUD, WS trusted-identity share/unshare in `test_playwright_ws_identity.py`, and `/etc/passwd` path-traversal rejection in `test_playwright_run_picker.py`). A commit pushed directly to `main` that breaks any of these passes CI green. Branch protection is unavailable on this repo's plan (API returns 403). *Adjusted to medium because PRs do run E2E — the regression only lands on a direct auth-breaking push to main, not in the normal flow.* **Fix:** run the E2E job (or at least the auth/ws-identity/picker subset) on push to main.

#### M2 — Project directories created under shared global work_dir, not per-user home
**File:** `home.py:530-573`. Project creation confines only with `validate_save_path` (permits anywhere under global `config.work_dir`); it never places the project under `user_data_root/{username}`. This is what makes H1 cross-user: every user's data co-locates under one root, and project dirs can collide/nest. **Fix:** derive the project root from `User.home_dir(config.user_data_root)`; reject names that escape or collide. (Fix jointly with H1.)

#### M3 — Unauthenticated WS sessions admitted from loopback in proxied server mode
**File:** `session_auth.py:618-639`. When `root_path` is set, any WS whose TCP peer is `127.0.0.1`/`::1` is admitted with `user=None` instead of closing with 4001 (justified because Shiny Server's internal WS drops the cookie). Any local process/co-tenant reaching the worker's WS port over loopback gets a live session with no credentials. Blast radius is limited — `current_user()` is then `None` and every server-mode gate is fail-closed — so this is defense-in-depth, and the peer is the real TCP peer (`scope['client']`, not XFF-spoofable), hence not remotely exploitable. **Fix:** keep as defense-in-depth, add a regression test asserting a localhost `user=None` WS can neither read `load_project_context` nor pass `editor_denied_reason`; long-term forward the token through the proxy.

#### M4 — validate_path resolves symlinks only when the target exists (TOCTOU/escape)
**File:** `config.py:285-308`. `resolve(strict=True)` runs only when `resolved.exists()`; for not-yet-existing write targets the allowlist check runs on the lexically-resolved path. An intermediate symlink pointing outside the roots lets a non-existent leaf pass `startswith()` while the real write lands outside the sandbox (`validate_save_path` has the same pattern). **Fix:** resolve the nearest existing ancestor with strict symlink resolution and validate that against the (per-user) allowlist regardless of whether the leaf exists.

#### M5 — Server-mode job listing filters by ephemeral session_id, not user_id
**File:** `run.py:553-565`. Non-admins see only jobs whose `metadata.session_id` matches the *current* WS session, but ownership is persisted as `user_id`. Shiny Server regenerates `session_id` on reconnect, so after a reload a user's still-running/completed jobs vanish (only admin `show_all` recovers them); server restarts do the same. **Fix:** add a `user_id` filter to `JobQueue.list_jobs` (Local + Celery) and key the non-admin filter on authenticated `user_id`, falling back to `session_id` only in local mode.

#### M6 — GRD element records spanning continuation lines are silently dropped
**File:** `parser_grd.py:364-391`. Continuation handling exists only for line records (type 3, via `pending_line`). Element records (`node_ids = [int(parts[4+i]) for i in range(nvert)]`) are single-pass with only a `len(parts) < 7` guard; a quad (nvert=4) or wrapped element raises `IndexError`, swallowed by the outer `except`, dropping the element. This corrupts `num_elements` and the downstream solver recommendation with only a buried `parse_warning`. **Fix:** apply the same pending/continuation accumulation to element records.

#### M7 — str_validator skips numeric checks for quoted timing values
**File:** `str_validator.py:18-68`. `apply_quick_settings` writes `itanf/itend/idt/idtout` quoted (e.g. `"'30'"`); `_get` tries `int`/`float`, both raise on the quotes, returning the raw string, so `isinstance(idt,(int,float))` is False and `idt > 0`, `itend > itanf` etc. are all skipped. A user can save `idt='0'` with no error. **Fix:** strip surrounding quotes in `_get` before conversion.

#### M8 — Workflow templates with unresolved step-output refs passed verbatim to tool
**File:** `workflow.py:536-568`. `_resolve_args` substitutes `{step.output_files[N]}` only when the prior step produced output; if not, the literal token is handed to the next tool as a filename, failing confusingly instead of aborting with a clear "previous step produced no output". No check for leftover `{...}`. **Fix:** detect remaining `{...}` after substitution and fail the step/workflow.

#### M9 — Preflight validation swallows all exceptions, reports clean
**File:** `run_logic.py:32-37`. `_preflight_validate` wraps the call in `except (ValueError, Exception): return []` (no logging). `Exception` subsumes `ValueError`, and any validator failure becomes an empty list — identical to "validation passed" — so a broken validator silently reports OK. Blast radius is currently limited (only a test-only re-export imports it). **Fix:** catch only the specific exception, or if keeping a safety net, `logger.warning(..., exc_info=True)` and return a sentinel warning.

#### M10 — Synchronous DB writes block the asyncio event loop
**File:** `job_local.py:280,286,367,122-155`. `_execute_job` (async, shared loop) calls fully synchronous `_persist_job` (blocking SQLAlchemy) ≥3× per job, plus `_delete_job_rows`/`cleanup_old_jobs`. The completion email was offloaded with `asyncio.to_thread` (line 372) but DB persistence was not; with the pooled production engine (`pool_pre_ping=True`, possibly remote) a slow commit/lock-wait stalls the loop, freezing every other session. **Fix:** wrap the sync DB calls in `await asyncio.to_thread(self._persist_job, job)`.

#### M11 — audit_logs table has no retention/pruning
**File:** `audit_service.py:1-117`. Rows written on every login/logout/admin op; the service exposes only insert/list/count/distinct, and `maintenance.py` prunes only jobs and expired sessions. Unbounded growth with indexed columns. **Fix:** add `AuditService.prune(older_than_days)` wired into `run_maintenance_once` with a configurable retention.

#### M12 — project_permissions FK has no ondelete/cascade → delete fails or orphans
**File:** `models/project.py:25-59`. FK enforcement is ON (`PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`, db/base.py:53) and no migration sets `ondelete`. `Project` declares delete-orphan cascade for grids/simulations/files but not `project_permissions`; `Workflow.project_id` (workflow.py:45) is a plain `Integer` with no FK at all. Latent today (no `delete_project()` exists), but the first delete path will `IntegrityError` on permissions and dangle workflows. **Fix:** add a `ProjectPermission` cascade relationship (and NULL/cascade workflows) before any delete feature; mirror `delete_user`'s manual cleanup.

#### M13 — Default database_url is a relative path resolving to the production DB
**File:** `config.py:48-49`. `default="sqlite:///./shyfem_ui.db"` is the prod DB, relative to CWD. Tests are protected by conftest (71-72), but an ad-hoc script/REPL/future test bypassing the fixture writes straight into prod, and the location silently moves with CWD. **Fix:** resolve the default to an absolute path anchored to the app data/work dir; keep conftest isolation.

#### M14 — E2E job masks flaky/failing browser tests with `--reruns 2`
**File:** `ui-ci.yml:89`. `pytest tests/test_playwright_*.py --reruns 2 --reruns-delay 3` reports a test green if it passes on retry. For the security/auth E2E this hides a probabilistic privilege-check failure as transient flake. **Fix:** run the auth/identity security E2E (`test_playwright_auth.py`, `test_playwright_ws_identity.py`) without reruns, or fail the job if a security test needs a rerun; surface rerun counts.

#### M15 — SPARSKIT `spk_solve_system`/mod_system use bare `stop` in MPI paths
**File:** `src/shyfem/sparskit_admin.f90:79,82,185,187,189,191,225,249,331` (and `mod_system_matrix.f90:175,232,…`). The default solver uses bare `stop` for MPI-reachable conditions — allocation failure, dimension overflow (223-226), and most importantly solver-failure (`if(ipar(1)<0) stop` at 329-332). Per convention, MPI paths must call `shympi_abort_internal`; a single rank diverging and stopping leaves peers blocking forever in the next collective. **Fix:** replace bare `stop` with `shympi_abort_internal(...)` in MPI-capable solver/assembly paths.

#### M16 — Bare `stop` inside MPI time-loop in conz3d_nodes deadlocks the run *(adj. high→medium)*
**File:** `src/shyfem/concentration_omp.f90:858,897`. `conz3d_nodes` (live path via conz3d_omp, called inside scal3sh's collective `do isact` loop with `shympi_exchange_3d_node` after each substep) has data-dependent bare stops: the loading internal-error check (858) and singular-tridiagonal `diag==0` check (897). These are per-node local conditions; firing on one rank leaves peers deadlocked at the next exchange. `shympi_abort_internal` is already in scope. *Adjusted to medium: both are degenerate-error guards, so the deadlock only manifests on an already-faulting run.* **Fix:** replace these and the other runtime stops in conz3d_omp (186,197,201,205,209,213,241,438,753) with `shympi_abort_internal`.

#### M17 — Negative-scalar clamp destroys mass; diagnostic is dead code
**File:** `src/shyfem/concentration.f90:747-753`. For non-temp scalars, `where(cnv < 1.e-15) cnv = 0.` floors *all* negatives (positivity undershoots) to zero with no redistribution — non-conservative whenever transport undershoots. The next line `if(any(cnv < 0.))` can never be true (all negatives just zeroed), so the negative-concentration diagnostic is unreachable dead code, masking the violation magnitude. **Fix:** move the `any(cnv<0.)` diagnostic *before* the floor; floor only tiny positive noise (`where(cnv>0. .and. cnv<1.e-15) cnv=0.`); if clamping negatives is required, account for the removed mass.

#### M18 — conz3d_element returns silently on allocation failure → wrong assembled system
**File:** `src/shyfem/concentration_omp.f90:447-450`. On allocation failure the routine prints and `return`s. Since it scatter-adds into shared `cn/cdiag/clow/chigh`, an early return drops that element's contribution; the global tridiagonal system is then missing terms and the solve yields silently wrong concentrations. The failure is swallowed inside an OMP TASK. **Fix:** abort (`shympi_abort_internal`) on failure; better, hoist the fixed-size scratch arrays to module/threadprivate save buffers allocated once.

#### M19 — weutro STEELE light formula drops layer-thickness factor *(adj. high→medium)*
**File:** `src/contrib/ecological/weutro/weutro.f90:1831-1840`. STEELE is the unconditional default (LGHTSW=3, param_init:306). The optical depth is computed `temp1 = ske*h` (1831) then dead-stored `temp1 = ske` (1832, `$WRONG_FORMULA`), so `temp3 = exp(-ske)` is dimensionally wrong (should be `exp(-ske*h)`). The surviving final line (1840) still consumes `temp3`, so the h-drop propagates into the phytoplankton growth multiplier (`GIT1 = RLIGHT*GITMAX`). The sibling DITORO/SMITH formulations were fixed to `TEMP1 = max(SKE*H, 1.e-10)`; only STEELE retains the override — a clear regression. *Adjusted to medium: the real 3D driver (bio3d.f90:562) supplies vertical light structure itself via Beer-Lambert, and iseg=1/ito=0 make the inter-layer chain inert, so impact is bounded to the within-layer growth-limitation error.* **Fix:** remove the `temp1=ske` dead store; choose explicitly between the depth-integrated and 2D Steele forms and delete the unused one.

#### M20 — weutro inter-layer light chain is dead in the 3D coupling
**File:** `src/contrib/ecological/weutro/weutro.f90:673-675`. `source()` hardcodes `iseg=1, ito=0` every call, so `RLGHTS(ITO,2)` writes a dummy slot and `RLGHTS(ISEG,2)` stays 1 — the surface-to-bottom attenuation chain never carries between layers. The only vertical light structure comes from `bio3d.f90:562` `qrad_l = qrad*exp(-ke_bg*depth_top)`, which uses *background* extinction only and excludes algal self-shading (KESHD), so deeper layers see too much light at high biomass. The comments at 1683-1685 describe the now-defunct chain and are misleading. **Fix:** accumulate algal self-shading into the inter-layer attenuation in bio3d, or wire ISEG/ITO so the light routines' RLGHTS chain is used per layer; update the stale comments.

#### M21 — Bare `stop` in active mercury sediment code paths *(adj. high→medium)*
**File:** `src/contrib/ecological/mercury/merc_sed4sed.f90:319,322,332,335,363`. Live bare `stop` statements fire when a node's sediment silt/POM goes ≤0 after the Euler update (called from `mercury.f90:554` inside `do k=1,nkn`). In MPI, `nkn` is per-rank, so a stop on one rank's node has no coordinated shutdown; even serial it kills a multi-day run with no checkpoint. Same in `merc_sed.f90:469,474,498,503` and `merc_water4sed.f90:188,192`. *Adjusted to medium: doubly opt-in (`MERCURY=true` at build + `imerc>0` at runtime), absent from default/verified build.* **Fix:** replace with `shympi_abort_internal`, or (preferred for a recoverable positivity violation) clamp to a small positive floor and continue.

#### M22 — merc_euler has no positivity floor; negatives clamped only for C(1) *(adj. high→medium)*
**File:** `src/contrib/ecological/mercury/mercury.f90:800-810`. `merc_euler`/`merc_euler_sed` do a bare `c(i)=(mass+dt*mder)/vol` with the floor commented out (809). In `merc_water.f90` only C(1)=Hg0 is clamped (457); C(2)=HgII and C(3)=MeHg negatives are merely printed (448-454) and passed unchanged into `scal_adv`. Negative dissolved/methyl mercury advected through the domain corrupts the mass balance. The first-order sinks in CD(2)/CD(3) (386-387) under a daily Euler step can drive these negative. *Adjusted to medium: optional opt-in mercury module.* **Fix:** add a uniform `c(i)=max(c(i),cmin)` floor in `merc_euler`/`_sed`, or clamp C(2)/C(3) alongside C(1); mirror the weutro `cmin`/`eutro_check` approach.

#### M23 — merc_water.f90 has zero intent attributes and hardcoded output units
**File:** `src/contrib/ecological/mercury/merc_water.f90:416,420,469-543`. No `intent(...)` on any argument (grep returns 0) on a kernel that mutates `c(:)`. Diagnostics write to hardcoded units (445, 448, and 350-382 selected by hardcoded external node ids 3985,3986,… in a long ladder) every timestep — collision risk with `newunit=` and a non-portable research artifact. Same hardcoded-unit pattern in `merc_sed.f90`/`merc_sed4sed.f90` (997/998/999). **Fix:** add intent attributes; replace hardcoded write units with `open(newunit=...)` gated behind a debug flag; remove the basin-specific node-id ladders.

#### M24 — Bare `stop` on allocation failure throughout MPI collective/exchange routines *(adj. high→medium)*
**File:** `src/utils/shympi/mpi_node_internal.f90` (25 sites: 352, 538, 540, 643, 645, 744, 746, 856, 858, 961, 963, 1070, 1072, 1179, 1181, 1288, 1290, 1397, 1399, 1479, 1520, 1561, 2177, 2214, 2251). Each is `if(ierr/=0) stop 'error stop: allocation failed'` inside collective ghost-exchange/allgather/gather routines (e.g. 538/540 precedes `MPI_Irecv/Isend/WaitAll` at 558-573; 1479/1520/1561 precede `MPI_ALLGATHER`). Fortran `STOP` terminates only the local image, so an allocation failure on one rank leaves peers blocking forever. `shympi_abort_internal` is the sanctioned idiom used in the *same* routines for other guards (1475/1516/1557), proving the bare `stop` is an inconsistency. *Adjusted to medium: the trigger is OOM of typically small buffers — rare.* **Fix:** replace every such `stop` with `call shympi_abort_internal(...)`.

#### M25 — Ghost-exchange point-to-point calls do not check `ierr`
**File:** `src/utils/shympi/mpi_node_internal.f90:558-573, 764-779, 2067-2080, 2128-2150`. `shympi_exchange_internal_i/_d` and both `shympi_get_array_internal_r/_i` issue `MPI_Irecv/Isend/WaitAll` and never test `ierr` (nor the per-request status error fields), unlike `shympi_receive_internal_r` (466-488), which checks and aborts. A truncated/failed halo transfer proceeds silently, corrupting ghost-node values. **Fix:** add `if(ierr/=0) call shympi_abort_internal('… MPI error')` after each call, mirroring the receive helper.

#### M26 — Inconsistent buffer-size strategy between int/double and real exchanges
**File:** `src/utils/shympi/mpi_node_internal.f90:535-549 vs 640-659`. `_i`/`_d` size message counts from the *local* `il(k)` level count (`count_buffer`), which must match the peer exactly. The `_r` variant was hardened to size every message to the fixed global maximum and assert `nbs(1)==nbs(2)` (654-658). The `_i`/`_d` paths keep the unguarded local-count scheme, so an `il` inconsistency that `_r` catches instead produces a silent size mismatch (compounded by M25). **Fix:** apply the same global-max sizing + `nbs(1)==nbs(2)` assertion to `_i`/`_d`, or add an explicit equality check before send/recv.

#### M27 — Non-deterministic global reductions use MPI_SUM on floats
**File:** `src/utils/shympi/mpi_node_internal.f90:1777,1807`. `shympi_reduce_internal_r/_d` do `MPI_ALLREDUCE(...,MPI_SUM,...)` over real/double scalars; MPI sum is not order-associative, so global sums (volume/mass/energy diagnostics) differ bit-for-bit by rank count/reduction tree, breaking run-to-run reproducibility and the MPI-vs-serial verification the project relies on. Single-precision `MPI_REAL` sums also lose accuracy. **Fix:** accumulate sums in double precision and document non-reproducibility across rank counts; if bit-reproducibility is required, gather-and-sum in a fixed canonical order on one rank.

#### M28 — allocate() without stat= in NUOPC cap and PETSc-global resize paths
**File:** `src/shyfem/mod_petsc_global.f90:369,374` (+ 5 in `nuopc_shyfem_cap.f90`, one each in `connections.f90` and `lagrange_mpi.f90:410`). Unchecked allocations in resize helpers abort with no diagnostic on failure. **Fix:** add `,stat=ierr` and an `if(ierr/=0)` guard (diagnostic + `shympi_abort_internal` in MPI paths).

#### M29 — angle() lacks div-by-zero norm guard and acos-arg clamp → NaN
**File:** `src/utils/generic/geometrical.f90:347-350`. `aux = (dx1*dx2+dy1*dy2)/norm` divides by `norm = sqrt(...)`, which is zero for a degenerate element (coincident vertices) → SIGFPE; `acos(aux)` is unclamped, so rounding can push `aux>1` → NaN. The sibling at 847 documents "arg in [-1,+1]", showing the guard is expected. **Fix:** `if(norm<=0.) return defined value; aux=max(-1.d0,min(1.d0,aux)); ang=acos(aux)*rad`.

#### M30 — COARE bulk flux divides by friction velocity usr=0 in calm wind
**File:** `src/shyfem/heat_coare.f90:801-802`. `usr=.035*u10` then `zo10 = 0.011*usr*usr/grav + 0.11*visa/usr`; for `u10→0`, `usr→0` and `0.11*visa/usr` divides by zero (SIGFPE under `-ffpe-trap`, or Inf into `log(10/zo10)`). The divisor recurs at 858/860. Coastal/lagoon runs routinely hit near-zero wind. **Fix:** floor `u10`/`usr` (`max(u10,umin)`) before any `1/usr` term.

#### M31 — Bare `stop` in MPI-active turbulence/chezy routines
**File:** `src/shyfem/turbulence.f90:113,340,431,437,1150` (and `chezy.f90:389,523,544`). Both files `use shympi` and call collective ops (e.g. `shympi_max`, `shympi_exchange_3d_node`), yet abort error paths with bare `stop` (e.g. `if(areakv(lmin,k)<=0.) stop` at 1150). One rank stopping while others wait in a collective deadlocks. **Fix:** replace with `shympi_abort_internal(...)`.

#### M32 — Uninitialized var as printf arg with caller string as format in Error()
**File:** `src/tools/femutil/unform/unformatted.c:486-491`. `Error(int ier, char *string)` calls `fprintf(stderr, string, dummy)` with `dummy` uninitialized and `string` as the format. Reading `dummy` is UB; any caller string containing a conversion specifier consumes garbage varargs (crash/info leak). Works today only because callers pass `%`-free literals. **Fix:** `fputs(string, stderr)` or `fprintf(stderr, "%s", string)`; drop `dummy`.

#### M33 — realloc self-assignment leaks + unchecked NULL deref in PsInitColorTable
**File:** `src/tools/postscript/psgraph.c:657-665`. `CT1 = realloc(CT1, size*sizeof(float))` (and CT2/CT3): on failure returns NULL, leaking the original, and the immediately following loop writes `CT1[i]=0.` through NULL → segfault; `size*sizeof(float)` has no overflow guard. **Fix:** realloc into a temporary, NULL-check before assigning/using, validate `size>0` with overflow-safe arithmetic.

#### M34 — bump-version.sh stages README.md but never modifies it
**File:** `bin/bump-version.sh:172`. The release commit does `git add … README.md`, but the script never edits README (badge updated manually). Any in-progress README edits are swept into the `release:` commit and captured under the tag, corrupting provenance; on a clean repo the line is useless. **Fix:** remove README.md from the `git add`, or edit it explicitly first.

#### M35 — bump-version.sh tags even when commit skipped
**File:** `bin/bump-version.sh:170-183`. Commit and tag are gated independently. `bump-version.sh minor --no-commit` (no `--no-tag`) rewrites files, skips the commit, but still runs `git tag -a vX.Y.Z` against the previous HEAD — an annotated tag pointing at a commit that lacks the bump, with the bumped files dirty in the tree. **Fix:** refuse to tag when no commit was made (force `NO_TAG=true` and warn when `NO_COMMIT`), or tag only the just-created commit.

---

### Low

- **L1 — Attacker/file-controlled record length drives malloc/fread** *(adj. high→low)* — `src/tools/femutil/unform/unformatted.c:232-476`. `read_record` reads `nrec1` from the file header unsanitized → `alloc_buffer(malloc(nbytes))`/`fread(...,nbytes,...)`; a huge value → unbounded malloc, a negative → `(size_t)negative`; `read_record_64` truncates the 8-byte length to int. *Low because these are offline diagnostic CLI tools with no privilege boundary — DoS on malformed input, not RCE.* Fix: reject negative/oversized lengths, use `size_t`, avoid the LONGLONG→int truncation.
- **L2 — home_dir escape guard uses startswith()** — `models/user.py:63-67`. `str(result).startswith(str(root))` treats `/data/users-evil` as inside `/data/u`. Not currently exploitable (admin.py validates usernames `^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]{1,64}$`), but `AuthService.create_user/ensure_user` accept arbitrary usernames programmatically. Fix: use `result.relative_to(root)` / `root in result.parents`.
- **L3 — GET /logout has no CSRF protection** — `session_auth.py:569-580`. State-changing logout exposed as GET with no token, unlike POST /login. A cross-site `<img>`/`<iframe>` can force logout (DoS/annoyance only). Fix: make logout POST with double-submit CSRF; confirm SameSite=Lax.
- **L4 — Audit-log client IP trusts X-Forwarded-For unconditionally** — `session_auth.py:659-673`. `_client_ip()` returns the first XFF value with no trusted-proxy check, so audit IPs are forgeable (audit-integrity only; not access control). Fix: reuse `rate_limit.get_client_ip(scope, config.trusted_proxies)`.
- **L5 — Anonymous feedback endpoint lacks email/content validation** — `feedback_service.py:63-65`. Only length-clipped; returned verbatim by admin GET JSON. Acceptable today (admin consumes JSON), but stored-XSS if a future admin view renders via `ui.HTML`. Fix: validate email format, reject control chars, keep a regression test asserting future views escape.
- **L6 — Time-series header detection breaks on leading blank line** — `timeseries_loader.py:78-99`. The header heuristic uses `i == 0` over enumerate-of-all-lines (including skipped blanks), so a leading blank line makes the real header `i>=1`, the header check never runs, and the row is dropped, losing column labels. Fix: track the first non-blank row.
- **L7 — run_shyfem mutates the caller's options list** — `shyfem_wrapper.py:365-366`. `args_list = options or []` then `.append(str_file)`, unlike sibling wrappers that copy. Reused option lists accumulate the str_file path across submissions. Fix: `args_list = list(options) if options else []`.
- **L8 — GRD parser silently drops node IDs in optional fields** — `parser_grd.py:311-315,380-383`. Two spots `pass` on `ValueError` without a `parse_warning`; the continuation-node pass can produce a line/boundary record with fewer nodes than declared, altering topology silently. Fix: append a `parse_warnings` entry in the continuation-node branch.
- **L9 — _load_history_from_db blocks during sync queue construction** — `job_local.py:74-96`. Synchronous query of up to 500 rows in `__init__` (app.py:275). Acceptable at startup but shares the sync-DB-in-singleton concern; a locked DB delays server availability. Fix: acceptable; if startup latency matters, lazy-load/bound with a timeout.
- **L10 — feedbacks table has no retention** — `feedback_service.py:31-78`. Anonymous insert per submission, no delete/retention anywhere; rate-limit only slows growth. Fix: add an optional terminal-status retention sweep; confirm the rate limit persists across restarts.
- **L11 — Coverage measured but never enforced** — `ui-ci.yml:56-59`. No `--cov-fail-under` anywhere; new (incl. write/auth) handlers can land at zero coverage, and an unlisted handler is invisible to both guard tests and coverage. Fix: add `--cov-fail-under=<N>`; fail CI when a new state-mutating handler is missing from `WRITE_HANDLERS`.
- **L12 — Picker security E2E silently skip if test hook disappears** — `tests/test_playwright_run_picker.py:50-51`. Path-traversal tests `pytest.skip` if `window.__test_set_active_project` is absent; a refactor dropping the hook turns every traversal assertion into a silent skip (green CI). Same in the other `*_picker.py` files. Fix: convert the missing-hook case to `pytest.fail`.
- **L13 — AST guard tests prove the guard is CALLED, not that it denies** — `tests/test_pages_access_control.py:316-358`. Static AST analysis only; runtime semantics covered for the gate in isolation and full wiring only by PR-only E2E, so on a push to main the write-handler privilege boundary is never exercised end-to-end. Fix: add a few in-process integration tests invoking page server functions with viewer/None identity in server mode.
- **L14 — mod_system module subroutine args lack intent(...)** — `src/utils/modules/mod_system_matrix.f90:154-403`. None of `mod_system_init/realloc2d/amat_init/insert_elem_index/set_local/global` declare intent on dummy args. Fix: scalars `intent(in)`, matrix `intent(inout)`, `nen3v intent(in)`.
- **L15 — Integer `afix` compared against real literal** — `src/shyfem/hydrodynamic.f90:1504-1506`. `afix` (integer, decl 1070) tested `if(afix /= 0.)`; works via implicit promotion but masks intent. Fix: `if(afix /= 0)`.
- **L16 — mod_system_realloc2d: real literal to int array + c2coo not preserved** — `src/utils/modules/mod_system_matrix.f90:314,321,328-330`. `iaux = 0.` (real literal into int array) and `c2coo` reallocated without copy-back (unlike i2coo/j2coo). Benign today (re-zeroed by `spk_init_system`) but an asymmetry that will lose data if realloc moves after assembly. Fix: `iaux = 0`; copy or document c2coo.
- **L17 — Hardcoded I/O unit numbers in concentration routines** — `src/shyfem/concentration_omp.f90:340,959` (also `concentration.f90:645,1021`). `990+my_id`, `789`, `888+my_id` instead of `newunit=`. Fix: `open(newunit=iu,…,iostat=ierr)` with checks, or gate behind a managed info-unit.
- **L18 — Unused double-precision `co` array allocated/copied every transport call** — `src/shyfem/concentration_omp.f90:174-354`. `co(nlvddi,nkn)` filled `co=cn1` every call, never read, then deallocated (header flags it `!not used !FIXME`); a wasted 8·nlvddi·nkn-byte copy per substep, and the per-call alloc/dealloc defeats the save caching. Fix: remove the `co` alloc/copy/dealloc; drop the DEALLOCATE of the saved cn/cdiag/clow/chigh buffers.
- **L19 — scalar_info_stability omits MPI reduction on stability index** — `src/shyfem/stability.f90:310-311`. The diagnostic variant recomputes `rindex/istot` without `shympi_max` (unlike the production path at 177), so on multi-rank runs the printed worst-node report reflects only the local subdomain at the moment of an abort. Fix: apply `rindex = shympi_max(rindex)` before scaling.
- **L20 — weutro source() hardcodes nstate=9 inconsistently** — `src/contrib/ecological/weutro/weutro.f90:362,646,397`. `nstate=9` redeclared as a local parameter in eutro0d/load0d/source/eutro_check rather than from the eutro module; a future change risks a slice mismatch with `e(:,:,nstate)` in bio3d. Fix: `use eutro, only: nstate` or pass as an argument.
- **L21 — to_buffer_r called with stale `nb` before nbs(2) assigned** — `src/utils/shympi/mpi_node_internal.f90:677-679,886-888`. `to_buffer_r(...,nb,...)` uses the leftover `nb` from the receive loop; `nb = nbs(2,ia)` is set only on the next line. Safe only because all nbs entries are forced equal. Fix: set `nb = nbs(2,ia)` before the call.
- **L22 — Copy-paste abort message in get_array_internal_r** — `src/utils/shympi/mpi_node_internal.f90:2055`. `shympi_get_array_internal_r` aborts with a message naming the `_i` routine, misdirecting diagnosis. Fix: correct the message to `_r`.
- **L23 — Bare `stop` in MPI debug routine check_2id_elements** — `src/shyfem/lnkmpi.f90:341`. Bare `stop` after `shympi_barrier`; all ranks reach it together (low deadlock risk) but it skips `MPI_FINALIZE` and violates convention. Fix: route through `shympi_finalize`/`shympi_stop`.
- **L24 — ~500 active GOTO statements remain** — `src/shyfem/matrix_inv.f90:195-280` (96 in file; also intp_fem_file.f90:56, heat_util.f90:48, nls.f90:25, topological.f90:22, femfile.f90:21). Genuine error-exit/loop jumps against the no-GOTO convention. Fix: convert to `if/exit/cycle`; for vendored LINPACK (matrix_inv.f90) relocate to `src/external` or replace with LAPACK rather than hand-restructuring numerically-sensitive code.
- **L25 — Three-line save+data init anti-pattern persists** — `src/shyfem/ous_admin.f90:96-97` (also stability.f90:563-564; 63 `data` statements across src). Fix: inline `integer, save :: x = v`; constant-table `data` (e.g. polynomial coefficients) may remain.
- **L26 — Locally-defined pi constant** — `src/utils/shyutil/evgeom.f90:755` (also projection.f90:89). Local `pi` parameters risk drift from `pi_dp/pi_sp`. Fix: `use mod_physical_constants, only: pi_dp` after confirming precision.
- **L27 — Local von Karman kappa=0.4 hardcoded in cdf()** — `src/shyfem/chezy.f90:419`. The module provides `vonkarman`; kepsilon.f90/heat_util2.f90 already use it. Fix: `use mod_physical_constants, only: vonkarman => vonkarman_sp`.
- **L28 — dist_point_to_line() divides by squared seg length, no zero guard** — `src/utils/generic/geometrical.f90:377-387`. `lambda = (rx*sx+ry*sy)/(rx*rx+ry*ry)`; for coincident A==B (duplicated grid nodes) → SIGFPE/NaN. Fix: `rr2=rx*rx+ry*ry; if(rr2<=0.) point-distance else divide`.
- **L29 — Centroid divides scaled sum with no zero-area guard** — `src/utils/generic/geometrical.f90:206-207`. `xc=xd/(3.*areasum)`; for a self-intersecting/zero-area polygon `areasum=0` → NaN centroid. Fix: fall back to vertex mean when `abs(areasum)<tiny`.
- **L30 — Fixed sprintf buffer s[20] can overflow for large %f values** — `src/tools/grid/gridma2.c:183,272-332`. `%f` for a value ≥~1e13 exceeds 20 bytes (GUI display path; small geographic coords in practice). Fix: `snprintf(s, sizeof(s), "%.6g", value)` or enlarge.
- **L31 — Unbounded strcat-of-extension chain into caller buffers** — `src/tools/mesh/meshgd.c:112-117` (also grdio.c:121). `makefilename` does `name = strcat(name,ext)` with no capacity knowledge; this is the mechanism that pushes the fixed `sfile[80]` callers past their end (compounds M-class gridfi.c overflow). Fix: pass the destination size and use `snprintf`/`strncat` with remaining-space accounting.
- **L32 — Dead "Rules.make cannot be read" guard** — `Makefile:25,37`. Default `RULES_MAKE_VERSION = 0.0` (unquoted) compared against quoted `"0.0"`, so the compatibility-skip branch never fires. Limited impact (Rules.make is committed and unconditionally included). Fix: compare against unquoted `0.0`.
- **L33 — SPEED/PGO profiles use -march=native** — `Rules.make:732-733`. `-O3 -march=native` targets the build host's exact CPU; a binary built on a newer node (AVX-512) SIGILLs on older deploy/run nodes — realistic since SHYFEM runs via mpirun across nodes and binaries are sometimes built-once-and-copied. Default NORMAL (`-O2`, no `-march=native`) is unaffected. Fix: offer a portable high-opt variant (`-march=x86-64-v3` or `-mtune=native`) and document the portability constraint.

#### Build/config — Intel MPI link footgun *(M-level, listed here for grouping with build items)*
**M36 — `make fem` silently links Intel MPI and crashes at MPI_Init** *(adj. high→medium)* — `Rules.make:750-753`. For an MPI build (repo defaults FORTRAN_COMPILER=GNU_GFORTRAN at 65 and PARALLEL_MPI=NODE at 114, so the out-of-the-box `make fem` *is* an MPI build), `FGNU=FGNU95=mpif90` is the bare PATH-resolved name. On the dev box Intel's `mpif90` is first, so the build compiles/links cleanly against Intel MPI then SIGFPEs in Intel's UCX at `MPI_Init` (or `PMPI_Barrier: Invalid communicator` with `I_MPI_FABRICS=shm`) because gfortran objects are incompatible with Intel's `mpi.mod`. No `which`/`command -v`/`--showme`/`ldd | grep libmpi.so.40`/`PATH=/usr/bin` guard exists anywhere in the build files. *Adjusted to medium: the crash is conditional on Intel shadowing OpenMPI in PATH (dev-box-specific); a clean OpenMPI-only host builds and runs fine.* **Fix:** add a make-time check that the resolved `mpif90` is OpenMPI (`mpif90 --showme:version` contains "Open MPI", or post-link `ldd $(EXE) | grep -q libmpi.so.40`), failing with a clear message; allow an explicit `MPIFC` override.

## 4. Refuted / false positives (appendix)

These were investigated and dismissed; listed so reviewers know coverage was real.

- **Job isolation keyed by `str(id(session))` → cross-user job exposure/cancellation** (`pages/run.py`). **Refuted.** The `session_id` filter only controls which jobs are *displayed*; it is not the authorization boundary. Every cancel/read site re-fetches the job and authorizes via `job_cancel_denied_reason`/`job_read_denied_reason` (access_control.py:75-129) against the WS-validated `current_user().id` / admin / project-editor. The disconnect-time `cancel_active_jobs_for_session` address-reuse path is unreachable because the session object is held alive by progress-callback/on_ended closures until the WS ends, by which point its own `on_ended` already cancelled its active jobs. `str(id(session))` is at most a code-quality nit; the claimed high-severity cross-user impact does not hold.

- **Bare `stop` in MPI-coupled `lnkmpi.f90` (deadlock at the headline location)**. **Refuted as headline.** The cited `stop` at `lnkmpi.f90:341` is inside `check_2id_elements`, documented "not yet finished", whose only call site (line 157) is **commented out** — dead scaffolding, cannot execute. Even hypothetically, lines 339-340 are `shympi_barrier` + `flush(6)` before the uniform `stop`, structurally preventing the claimed partial-halt deadlock. (The general theme survives elsewhere — see M15/M16/M24/M31/L23 — but not at this anchor; the still-live `lnkmpi.f90:341` convention nit is captured as L23.)

- **cdf() friction division-by-zero when bottom roughness z0 reaches zero** (`src/shyfem/chezy.f90`). **Refuted.** The code smell is real (no floor on `z0`, unlike turbulence.f90:484), but none of the three claimed z0=0 input paths is reachable under default/documented config: `ireib=6` `czv` is validated strictly positive by `ckarea` (which `stop`s at chezy.f90:1040 for zero); the `ireib=8` `z0bk` write-back in sedim_admin.f90:1773 is **commented out** and `z0bini=9e-4>0`; `ireib=9` uses `alpha=1.` (stub) × positive `czv`. The only residual trigger is an exotic deliberate misconfiguration. Downgraded to a defensive-hardening nit, not a triggerable SIGFPE.

---

## 5. Coverage & method

**Areas reviewed.** The review spanned both halves of the codebase across the dimensions tagged in the findings:
- **Python UI (`shyfem-ui`):** web security / path confinement (`ui-websec`), authentication & authorization (`ui-auth`), data lifecycle & DB (`ui-data`), correctness (`ui-correctness`), error handling (`ui-errors`), reactive/async behavior (`ui-reactive`), and CI/test gaps (`ui-tests`).
- **Fortran core:** hydrodynamics & solver assembly (`f-hydro`), scalar transport (`f-transport`), numerics (`f-numerics`), the MPI layer (`f-mpi`), conventions (`f-conventions`), and the ecological contrib modules weutro/EUTRO and mercury (`f-eco`).
- **C utilities:** memory safety in the grid/mesh/postscript/femutil tools (`c-memory`).
- **Build system:** `Rules.make`, `Makefile`, `bump-version.sh`, and `ui-ci.yml` (`build-config`, `ui-tests`).

**Adversarial verification.** Every **high/critical** finding carries an explicit verifier verdict; each was an attempt to *refute* the finding by reading the actual code along multiple independent angles (e.g. the PETSc finding survived six refutation angles; the validate_path IDOR was checked against the access-control gate semantics and the prod topology). Six high-severity candidates were verifier-**downgraded to medium** (E2E-on-main gap, conz3d_nodes stop, weutro STEELE, mercury bare-stop, mercury Euler floor, MPI alloc-stop, gridfi.c overflow, Intel-MPI link) or **to low** (the femutil unformatted-reader length-validation bug), and three candidate highs were **fully refuted** (section 4). Medium and low findings were confirmed by direct code reading but were not run through the second adversarial pass.

**Sampled rather than exhaustively read.** A few findings are explicitly *confirmations of soundness* of high-risk surfaces (reported as low): the per-id `reactive.effect` dedup-guard pattern (home.py/files.py/boundary_editor.py) and the deferred connect-time `Shiny.setInputValue` in app.py were audited and found correct in the inspected instances — not a guarantee that every future handler follows suit. Convention-class Fortran findings (GOTOs ~500, `data`/`save` ~63, hardcoded units, local constants) were established by representative grep counts and spot-checked anchors rather than enumerating every occurrence. The duplicate C buffer-overflow sites in `meshfi.c`/`intgrd.c`/`spgrd.c`/`maskgrd.c`/`exgrd.c` were inferred from the shared pattern; only the `gridfi.c` anchor was line-verified. PETSc/NUOPC `stat=`-less allocations beyond the two cited lines, and the full mercury/weutro contrib trees, were sampled around the cited anchors rather than read in full.
